questions.q: How does the lesson say governance programs typically fail?
options: Quietly — budget keeps renewing and meetings continue while the underlying problems never go away
With a sudden, dramatic, visible collapse
Only when the company goes bankrupt
They never fail once funded
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes that failure is usually quiet and ongoing, not a dramatic visible event — which makes it harder to notice early.

questions.q: What is the early warning sign of 'tool-first thinking' per the lesson?
options: A tool is live and dashboards exist, but nobody can say who's accountable when the dashboard shows a problem
The organization refuses to buy any software at all
Executives personally review every data entry
The IT budget is reduced to zero
questions.explain: Tool-first thinking mistakes buying a catalog or quality tool for doing the harder work of defining ownership and decision rights.

questions.q: What happens, per the lesson, when there are no clear decision rights?
options: The same definitional disagreement resurfaces in meeting after meeting, never resolved
All disagreements are automatically escalated to the CEO
Data quality instantly improves
Departments stop communicating entirely
questions.explain: Without a defined process and authority to resolve disagreements, they simply persist indefinitely rather than getting settled.

questions.q: What does the lesson say is the common thread across all five failure patterns?
options: They are organizational failures — sponsorship, structure, and measurement — not technology gaps
They all stem from insufficient server capacity
They only happen in small organizations
They are caused by using open-source software
questions.explain: None of the five patterns involve a technology gap; they're about sponsorship, structure, decision rights, and measurement — which is why the course focuses on those, not tools.

questions.q: Per the lesson, what is the warning sign that governance has become 'disconnected from business value'?
options: At budget season, no one outside the data organization can articulate what the governance program actually did for them
The program has too many executive sponsors
Data quality scores are too high
The governance council meets too frequently
questions.explain: This failure mode measures itself by internal activity (policies written, meetings held) rather than any outcome the rest of the business recognizes or values.
